newCards.flavor: Behind the armory, three soldiers dice for a fallen sentry's boots while his body lies under a blanket a few steps away. His younger sister waits barefoot by the ditch with her arms wrapped around herself. The dice are bone, and one of them keeps landing on six.

choices.label: Join the game for the boots
choices.intent: Buy into the game and beat the loaded die at its own trick.
choices.risk: Men who cheat at dice do not like losing.

success.text: You swap their loaded die for an honest one while they argue over the pot, and you win the boots on the second throw. You carry them to the sister, who puts them on at once. The soldiers grumble, but none of them will admit to the die.

failure.text: They catch your hand on the die before you can swap it. They keep your stake, shove you into the ditch, and go back to their game while the sister watches you climb out, muddy and sore.

choices.label: Shame them before the body
choices.intent: Lift the blanket from the sentry's face and ask which of them stood his last watch.
choices.risk: Grief and shame both come out as fists.

success.text: The dicing stops. The youngest soldier picks up the boots and takes them to the sister himself, and the others do not stop him. Nobody in the armory speaks to you again for the rest of the night.

failure.text: The oldest soldier hits you before you finish the sentence, and his friends hold you while he does it twice more. The boots stay in the pot, and the sister slips away into the dark before you can stand.

choices.label: Buy the boots outright
choices.intent: Offer the soldiers enough food for the boots to end the game.
choices.risk: They will remember you as someone who pays.

success.text: They take your food and split it before handing over the boots. The sister takes them without a word and walks off toward the refugee fires. Later you hear the soldiers dicing again, for something else of his.

newCards.title: The Wooden Horse at the Gate
newCards.flavor: A woman who once went beyond the gate and came back sits against the threshold wall, turning a carved wooden horse in her hands. She made it for her son, who waits in the camp a day behind you. She cannot make herself walk back and face his questions, and she will not say what she saw.

choices.label: Carry the horse to her son
choices.intent: Promise to take the horse back to the camp and put it in her son's hands.
choices.risk: A day back down the road is a day you walk twice.

success.text: You walk back down the black road, find the boy by the refugee fires, and put the horse in his hands. He asks where his mother is, and you tell him she is waiting at the gate. By the time you climb back to the threshold you are worn to the bone.

choices.label: Urge her to go herself
choices.intent: Tell her the boy needs his mother more than any answer she might owe him.
choices.risk: Push too hard, and she may break instead of bend.

success.text: She sits with it a long time, then stands, tucks the horse into her coat, and starts down the black road toward the camp. She does not thank you. At the bend she looks back once, her face wet and set.

failure.text: She hears an accusation in it and turns her face to the wall. When you finally leave, the horse is lying in the ash beside her, and you have sat with her so long that the cold has gotten into you.

choices.label: Ask what she saw beyond
choices.intent: Ask her, gently, what waits past the gate, so you can walk into it ready.
choices.risk: Some answers cost the one who gives them.

success.text: She is quiet so long you think she will not answer. Then she says only that the hardest part is the asking, and that you should keep your own words close. It is not much, but she holds your eyes while she says it.

failure.text: Your question opens something she had closed. She starts to shake and cannot stop, and you give her your blanket and the last of your warm tea before you leave her to it.

newCards.title: The Creditor's Tally Sticks
newCards.flavor: A creditor waits at the last gate with a bundle of notched tally sticks, buying debts from all over the road and collecting them before anyone passes beyond her reach. A family ahead of you owes her for seed grain bought in the drought. She has already taken their mule, and now she is counting their children's coats.

choices.label: Pay down their debt
choices.intent: Hand the creditor what food you can spare against the family's tally.
choices.risk: Debts like theirs rarely stay paid.

success.text: The creditor shaves two notches off their stick and hands the coats back. The father thanks you too many times. You go on toward the gate lighter than you should be, and the creditor is already turning to the next family.

choices.label: Match the two halves
choices.intent: Ask to lay her half of the tally beside the family's half, notch for notch.
choices.risk: She has done this far longer than you have.

success.text: Her half has three notches the family's half does not. You lay the two sticks side by side in front of the line, and the creditor, smiling thinly, calls it a clerk's mistake. She returns the mule and studies your face as you go.

failure.text: The halves match notch for notch; the debt is real. The creditor charges you for wasting her morning, and the family looks at you as if you have made it worse.

choices.label: Sign over a debt owed you
choices.intent: Someone on the road owes you; offer that debt to the creditor in place of theirs.
choices.risk: You will reach the end of the road owed nothing.

success.text: The creditor knows the name you give and likes the terms better. She breaks the family's tally stick across her knee and notches a fresh one for your debtor instead. Whatever was owed to you is hers to collect now.

choices.label: Walk past the creditor
choices.intent: Keep your head down and pass her table before she thinks to ask about you.
choices.risk: The children's coats will still be on her table.

success.text: You slip past while she is counting, and she does not stop you; your debts are not on her sticks. You hear the youngest crying for her coat until the shadow of the gate swallows the sound.

newCards.title: The Charcoal Portraits
newCards.flavor: A line of wardens in ash-grey coats checks every face at the threshold against a sheaf of charcoal portraits: deserters, thieves, troublemakers from the road. They have seized a young man who swears he is not the one drawn. The portrait in the warden's hand could be him, or half the people in line.

choices.label: Vouch for the young man
choices.intent: Tell the wardens you have walked beside him for days and he is no deserter.
choices.risk: A lie for a stranger is still a lie to wardens.

success.text: The warden studies you, then the portrait, then you again, and lets the young man go with a cuff on the ear. He does not know you and does not ask why you lied for him. The warden takes a long, careful look at your face.

failure.text: The young man contradicts you without meaning to, naming a village you have never seen. The wardens hold you both until dusk and take a share of your food as a fine before they let you go.

choices.label: Compare the face to the drawing
choices.intent: Look closely at the portrait for some detail the young man's face does not share.
choices.risk: If he is the one drawn, you have helped condemn him.

success.text: The drawing shows a notch in the left ear, and the young man's ears are whole. You point it out quietly, and the warden, annoyed but fair, lets him go. Later the young man finds you and shares a heel of bread from his pack.

failure.text: You find the notch in the drawing's ear, and the young man's ear has it too. As the wardens drag him off he kicks out and catches your shin, cursing you for looking, and you carry that through the gate.

choices.label: Keep your place in line
choices.intent: Stay quiet, show your face, and pass when your turn comes.
choices.risk: He will remember who looked away.

success.text: The warden glances from your face to his sheaf and waves you on. Behind you the young man is still insisting, louder now, and then not at all. Nobody on the far side of the line asks you anything.

choices.label: Give them a better face
choices.intent: The wardens already know your face; step forward and offer them yourself instead.
choices.risk: They will take what you offer, and maybe more.

success.text: The warden's eyes widen when he finds your portrait near the top of the sheaf. They let the young man go and keep you in the guardhouse overnight, asking the same questions with their fists. At dawn they shove you out toward the gate, sore all over and glad to be rid of you.

newCards.title: The Sentry Without Relief
newCards.flavor: An old sentry stands at the threshold in a coat patched so often it has no first color, spear grounded, ribs showing through his shirt. He swore to hold this post until his relief arrived, and that was forty winters ago. The lord who gave the order is long dead, and the sentry is starving within sight of the camp's cookfires.

choices.label: Stand his watch tonight
choices.intent: Take his spear for the night so he can eat and sleep without breaking his oath.
choices.risk: The cold at the threshold is worst before dawn.

success.text: He sleeps for the first time in years, curled against the wall, and you hold the post through a night so cold your fingers stop answering. At dawn he takes the spear back. It changes nothing, he says, but he says it gently.

choices.label: Tell him no one is coming
choices.intent: Tell him plainly that his lord is dead and no relief will ever climb this road.
choices.risk: An old soldier's oath may be all that holds him up.

success.text: He listens without moving. Then he lays the spear across the threshold, very carefully, as if it might wake, and starts down toward the cookfires on legs that shake. He does not look back at the post.

failure.text: He calls you a liar and levels the spear. You back away with a gash across your forearm, and he goes on standing his post, hungrier and lonelier than before you came.

choices.label: Leave food at his feet
choices.intent: Set your bread on the stones by his post, where he can reach it without moving.
choices.risk: Food will not relieve him; it only keeps him standing.

success.text: He waits until you have stepped back before he eats, and he eats like a man trying not to. He thanks you in an old, formal way and goes on standing exactly where he was.

choices.label: Swear the relief oath
choices.intent: You know what a kept promise costs; swear his relief in the old words and free him.
choices.risk: Swear it, and the oath is yours to carry.

success.text: He hears the old words in your voice and believes you, as he would believe no one else. He gives you the post's iron key and shows you the sentry stair inside the wall, which runs past the gate to ground no map shows, and the road ahead changes.

failure.text: You stumble over words no one has spoken in forty years, and he hears the mistake. He thanks you for trying and keeps his post. You sit with him a while and share what food you have before you go.

newCards.title: The Smuggler's Side Door
newCards.flavor: Far from the negotiator's gate, a smuggler keeps a narrow side door in the threshold wall and lets people through it for food. Her price buys one passage, not two. A refugee family with three children sits beside the door with nothing to pay, watching each person who can.

choices.label: Pay for your own passage
choices.intent: Pay the smuggler's price and go through the side door alone.
choices.risk: The family will watch you go.

success.text: The smuggler unbars the door, and a cold stone passage carries you out far from the main gate, where the road beyond runs differently than anyone told you. Behind you, the door closes on the family's faces.

choices.label: Pay for the family instead
choices.intent: Hand over the price for the family's passage and face the main gate yourself.
choices.risk: You will meet the negotiator with an emptier pack.

success.text: The smuggler counts the food twice and lets them through, the children ducking under her arm. The mother looks back from the dark of the passage as if to memorize you. Then the door closes, and you turn toward the main gate with almost nothing left.

choices.label: Haggle for a group price
choices.intent: Argue that an empty passage earns her nothing, and talk her into taking all of you.
choices.risk: She can close the door and wait for someone easier.

success.text: She laughs at your nerve and takes one ration for the lot of you. You all squeeze through the cold stone passage together, the children holding the back of your coat, and come out on a stretch of road beyond that you had never heard of.

failure.text: She takes your food as a fee for listening and closes the door. The family stays where they are, and so do you, with even less in your pack than before.

choices.label: Lead them by the old way
choices.intent: Skip the smuggler's door and lead the family along a hidden route you learned on the road.
choices.risk: Old ledges crumble, and children will be following you.

success.text: The old way is where you hoped: a buried ledge along the wall, marked with the worn signs you learned to read. You lead the family past the gate without paying anyone, and at the far end the father presses a twist of dried fish into your hand.

failure.text: The ledge has crumbled since the old signs were cut. You get the children back to the door safely, but you slip on the way down and land hard on the broken stone.

family-at-the-fence.label: Refill the child's bowl
family-at-the-fence.intent: Drink from the bowl, then fill it again from your own flask before you walk on.
family-at-the-fence.risk: You leave with less water, and maybe no shelter.

success.text: The girl watches you fill it to the brim. One of the grown-ups lets out a breath, and the eldest calls you back to sleep by the hearth. At dawn she wraps a few windfall apples for your road.

the-orchard-debt.label: Name your price first
the-orchard-debt.intent: Agree to help only after she promises a full share of the harvest.
the-orchard-debt.risk: A hard bargain before a storm sours the gratitude.

success.text: She meets your eye and agrees. You heave and sweat, and she pays exactly what she promised, counted out sack by sack, and does not say she will remember you.

failure.text: She calls you a road vulture and hauls the barrel up alone, inch by inch. You walk on empty-handed while the first rain hits the dust.

scarecrows-lantern.label: Leave bread under the lantern
scarecrows-lantern.intent: Set some of your food beneath the scarecrow for whoever is hungry enough to steal.
scarecrows-lantern.risk: The farmer may think you are feeding a thief.

success.text: You walk back to the road and wait. Near dawn a thin boy comes for the bread, eats half, and wraps the rest. He sees you and does not run; he raises one hand, and is gone.

scarecrows-lantern.label: Call out behind the barn
scarecrows-lantern.intent: Announce yourself loudly, so whoever waits there knows you mean no harm.
scarecrows-lantern.risk: Your voice may send someone running through their own snare.

success.text: A boy comes out with his hands up and the farmer's rations in his shirt. His family camps in a dry gully, and he shows you the path they took, a way the road ahead had kept hidden.

failure.text: Your voice sets something running. The thief bolts through his own snare line and drags the lantern down into the hay. You beat out the smoldering straw with your coat and burn your hands.

the-last-seed.label: Dig a catch basin
the-last-seed.intent: Spend the afternoon digging a hollow to catch the next rain for the shoot.
the-last-seed.risk: Hard labor in the heat, for rain that may not come.

success.text: You dig until your arms shake and the sun goes down. There is no rain, and there may not be for weeks, but the hollow is there. She thanks you, and you leave with nothing but sore hands.

the-last-seed.label: Trade for half her seeds
the-last-seed.intent: Offer her food for half her seeds, since seeds travel and her well will not last.
the-last-seed.risk: She may see it as robbery dressed up as trade.

success.text: She thinks about it a long time, then counts the seeds into your palm, half of the last she has. Your food goes down into her cellar. You carry her harvest east, whatever it becomes.

failure.text: She closes the tin and holds it to her chest. You have frightened her, and she will not look at you again. You leave with your food and the feeling that you took something anyway.

rope-at-dawn.label: Let the tired traveler drink first
rope-at-dawn.intent: Step back so the waiting traveler can drink before you, while the rope still holds.
rope-at-dawn.risk: The rope may part before your turn comes.

success.text: The tired stranger drinks, then drinks again. When your turn comes, the rope snaps and the bucket goes down for good. The keeper shares what is left in her own jug, one mouthful each, and you go on thirsty.

a-cup-offered.label: Compare herbs with her
a-cup-offered.intent: Open your own medicine pouch and trade what you know for what she knows.
a-cup-offered.risk: Herbalists guard their recipes like family silver.

success.text: She sniffs your herbs, nods at one, frowns at another. You trade a pinch of yours for a twist of her willow bark, and she names the roadside weeds that are safe to boil and eat.

failure.text: You show her a root she believes is poison, and she backs away as if you meant to dose her. She leaves the well without her cup and without another word.

a-cup-offered.label: Pour the cup out politely
a-cup-offered.intent: Refuse the drink with thanks and pour it out at the foot of the well.
a-cup-offered.risk: You may insult her, and lose a friend on the road.

success.text: She watches the water sink into the sand, then nods, as if you have told her something about yourself. She does not offer again, and she does not walk the road with you.

marks-below-water.label: Stand at the road and warn
marks-below-water.intent: Wave every cart to a stop and send them around the well until it is shored up.
marks-below-water.risk: A long day in the sun, waving at angry drivers.

success.text: You turn back nine carts before dusk, and one driver curses you all the way past. At sundown the rim stones slump an inch into the shaft. The road ahead now runs the long way around the well.

marks-below-water.label: Copy the carved circles
marks-below-water.intent: Trace the old circles onto cloth so someone who reads such things can explain them.
marks-below-water.risk: Lean too long over the shaft and the stones may go.

success.text: The circles nest inside each other like ripples, and the newest were scratched by a small hand. You fold the cloth into your pack. The longer you look at it, the less you like it.

failure.text: Your head swims as you lean over the water, and the circles seem to turn. You come back to yourself on the ground beside the rim, with a cut on your brow and an empty cloth.

two-empty-buckets.label: Keep the second bucket
two-empty-buckets.intent: Take the abandoned bucket for your own road, since no one has come for it.
two-empty-buckets.risk: Someone may still be coming back for it.

success.text: It is sound and tight, and you fill it to the brim with water for the road. The courier watches you take it and says nothing, and the next day she carries only one family's share.

two-empty-buckets.label: Ask the neighbors about them
two-empty-buckets.intent: Knock on nearby doors and ask when anyone last saw the missing household.
two-empty-buckets.risk: Frightened neighbors talk to each other, not to strangers.

success.text: An old man says the family went to the refuge after their mule died, and the sisters sent the parents on alone to find work. He points the way they went, and your road ahead turns with it.

failure.text: Doors open a hand's width and close again. Nobody wants to talk about the refuge to a stranger, and the long walk between farms leaves you footsore and no wiser.

gate-still-open.label: Ask after those you left
gate-still-open.intent: Ask the sister whether the people you walked away from on the road reached this gate.
gate-still-open.risk: The answer may be worse than not knowing.

success.text: She checks a list and says they came through and are safe. Then you notice she never turned the page, and you understand she tells everyone the same. You go in anyway and eat the hot stew.

failure.text: She says she remembers no one like that, and closes the gate on the question. You sit outside on the cold ground, thinking about the people you left behind, and do not sleep.

gate-still-open.label: Sleep outside the wall
gate-still-open.intent: Decline the bed with thanks and camp in the dust where you can watch the gate.
gate-still-open.risk: A cold night, and the sisters will take it as an insult.

success.text: The night is cold and gritty. Near midnight the gate opens for a covered cart that rolls out without a lantern and turns east. By morning you are stiff, and you know something they did not mean to show you.

the-locked-dormitory.label: Call in what you are owed
the-locked-dormitory.intent: Send word to someone who owes you to keep the senior sisters busy at the gate.
the-locked-dormitory.risk: If it goes wrong, you have spent a friend for nothing.

success.text: A commotion breaks out at the gate, and every senior sister goes to see it. You have one long, quiet minute at the keyhole, and you see a child's name chalked inside the door, half wiped away.

failure.text: The commotion comes too early. The corridor fills with sisters before you reach the door, and you leave the refuge having spent your favor on nothing.

the-locked-dormitory.label: Go back to the refectory
the-locked-dormitory.intent: Do as the novice asks, so no one punishes the novice for your curiosity.
the-locked-dormitory.risk: Whatever that room holds stays behind the door.

success.text: The novice's shoulders drop with relief. At supper a second bowl of stew appears at your elbow, and you eat it slowly, warming through, while the novice will not meet your eyes all evening.

a-crust-for-the-road.label: Ask what frightens her
a-crust-for-the-road.intent: Ask her quietly, away from the windows, why she keeps glancing back at the convent.
a-crust-for-the-road.risk: Your question could get her punished, not you.

success.text: She says the Abbess does not like bread leaving the kitchen, because bread is how the house counts who is fed. Then, very fast, she says the children's wing is fed last and least.

failure.text: She goes white, presses the parcel back into your hands, and hurries inside. Through the window you see a senior sister speak to her, and her head stays bowed.

a-crust-for-the-road.label: Give the parcel back
a-crust-for-the-road.intent: Return the bread so she is not caught giving away the kitchen's leftovers.
a-crust-for-the-road.risk: You walk on hungry, and her kindness goes unused.

success.text: She hesitates, then takes it back. Her face shows relief and disappointment at once. You leave with nothing from the kitchen, and you are not sure whether you spared her or refused her.

the-silent-bell.label: Strike the bell with a stone
the-silent-bell.intent: Climb partway and strike the bronze with a stone, to see who comes running.
the-silent-bell.risk: Everyone in the refuge will know it was you.

success.text: The bell gives one long note over the dust. Sisters spill into the courtyard, and in the confusion you see the Abbess at a high window, looking not at the bell but at the road east. Then you run.

failure.text: Your stone glances off and you lose your footing on the stair. You come down hard, and you are found sitting in the courtyard holding a rock, with no good story to tell.

the-silent-bell.label: Let the bell stay silent
the-silent-bell.intent: Thank the caretaker and leave the tower alone, since he seems afraid for his post.
the-silent-bell.risk: Whatever the silence hides stays hidden.

success.text: He sags with relief, fills your waterskin, and walks you to the gate himself, talking about anything but the bell. There he says the eastern road is longer but safer, and the way ahead changes.

lanterns-on-the-raft.label: Pay the family's passage
lanterns-on-the-raft.intent: Hold up a day's food as fare so the ferryman will bring the raft in for the family.
lanterns-on-the-raft.risk: He may take the fare and keep on circling.

success.text: The ferryman takes your food, poles in, and lifts the family aboard. Then he pushes off before you can step on, and you spend the afternoon on the bank waiting for his next pass.

lanterns-on-the-raft.label: Lead them to the old ford
lanterns-on-the-raft.intent: Walk the family upstream to a ford you know, where the river runs knee-deep.
lanterns-on-the-raft.risk: Old fords move, and the family is trusting you.

success.text: The ford is still there, braided and shallow. You carry the youngest across on your back while the ferryman watches from his raft, and on the far side the road ahead runs somewhere new.

failure.text: The ford has shifted downstream since you knew it, and the cold current knocks you to your knees mid-crossing. The family turns back to wait for the raft, and you come out soaked and shivering.

toll-of-two-names.label: Give a false name
toll-of-two-names.intent: Give the registrar a name that is not yours, and watch what she writes beside it.
toll-of-two-names.risk: Some ledgers remember faces better than names.

success.text: She writes the name and, beside it, the debt of a traveler lost last spring. You walk through knowing that whoever comes asking for that name will find nobody at all.

failure.text: She studies your face and crosses out the false name with one stroke. The guards walk you to the back of the queue, and the long wait costs you a meal you meant to save.

toll-of-two-names.label: Claim the wardens' business
toll-of-two-names.intent: The guards already know your face, so pose as warden business and demand the old pages.
toll-of-two-names.risk: Someone here may remember exactly where they saw you.

success.text: The guards hesitate, unsure what you are to them, and the registrar hands over the old pages to be rid of you. In the margin beside every repeated name is the toll keeper's mark.

failure.text: One guard remembers exactly where he saw your face, and it was not on warden business. They march you to the back of the queue with a fist in your ribs.

the-boat-that-waits.label: Pole the skiff across
the-boat-that-waits.intent: Cut the waiting skiff loose and cross in it before the boatwright can object.
the-boat-that-waits.risk: The rudder is half mended, and the owner may yet return.

success.text: The half-mended rudder holds long enough. You tie the skiff to a post on the far bank, and the boatwright's shouts carry across the water after you.

failure.text: Halfway across the rudder snaps and the skiff spins into a snag. You wade the rest of the way, bruised, your rations soaked, and watch the empty boat drift off downriver.

the-boat-that-waits.label: Leave food under the seat
the-boat-that-waits.intent: Tuck a day's food under the skiff's seat for whoever comes back, and walk on.
the-boat-that-waits.risk: No one may ever come for it.

success.text: The boatwright watches you do it and says nothing, but he walks you to the ferry and tells the pilot to let you ride. You never learn whether anyone came back for the boat.

weighed-in-salt.label: Share your salt down the line
weighed-in-salt.intent: Pour your own salt into the hands of the people at the back of the queue.
weighed-in-salt.risk: The merchant will notice someone with salt to spare.

success.text: It is only a pinch each, but the queue stands a little straighter. The merchant watches you do it and nudges his prices up again, as though your generosity proved you had money.

weighed-in-salt.label: Press a thumb under the pan
weighed-in-salt.intent: When the merchant turns to his ledger, press a thumb under the pan to tip it.
weighed-in-salt.risk: Cheating a cheat is still cheating, if he sees it.

success.text: Your thumb lifts the pan and the merchant pours a double measure without noticing. You walk out with salt and a heel of bread, past people who were not as quick as you.

failure.text: He catches your thumb under the pan and bends it back until you gasp. His hired hands toss you out the door, and the queue watches without any sympathy at all.

the-mended-compass.label: Draw a seventh map together
the-mended-compass.intent: Tell her every landmark you passed this morning and help her draw the river again.
the-mended-compass.risk: Your memory may be no steadier than her river.

success.text: Together you draw a seventh map, and for once she does not erase it. She gives you the copy, and the road ahead rearranges itself around channels neither of you had seen before today.

failure.text: Your memory and her drafts quarrel all afternoon, and the map you draw together is worse than either. She thanks you kindly, and you leave tired, with the light nearly gone.

three-cups-on-the-table.label: Drink the quiet cup
three-cups-on-the-table.intent: Lift the cup for whoever asks no questions, drink it down, and keep your eyes on the bowl.
three-cups-on-the-table.risk: Silence is also an answer here.

success.text: The patrons relax and turn back to their own bowls. The broth is hot and good, and you leave knowing nothing more than when you sat down, which seems to be what everyone wanted.

three-cups-on-the-table.label: Raise the lost traveler's cup
three-cups-on-the-table.intent: Lift the cup for the one who never came back, and drink it before the patrons.
three-cups-on-the-table.risk: The patrons may know exactly why that traveler did not return.

success.text: The patrons stiffen, and then one of them lowers his eyes. At the door the cook tells you the lost traveler was her son, and that he asked too many questions about the checkpoint downriver.

failure.text: One patron knocks the cup from your hand and grinds his boot onto your foot until you sit down. The cook will not meet your eyes after that, and you limp out alone.

footprints-in-the-silt.label: Walk him to high ground
footprints-in-the-silt.intent: Tell the surveyor the fresh mud means water tonight, and insist he climb out with you.
footprints-in-the-silt.risk: He will lose his line, and he may never forgive it.

success.text: He grumbles but comes, and from the high bank at dusk you watch the channel fill where his next stake would have stood. From up here you can see the new channels, and the road ahead will have to bend around them.

a-road-of-bones.label: Ask who laid the timbers
a-road-of-bones.intent: Press the guide gently about who built the road, and why she will not say.
a-road-of-bones.risk: She may take the question as a robber's question.

success.text: Her own people laid it, three generations back, to carry their dead to burial islands the river has since abandoned. Out of respect for the asking, she shows you the timbers that still bear weight and an old burial path that reshapes your road ahead.

failure.text: She takes it as a robber's question and leaves you at the edge of the inlet. You cross alone at dusk, and a splintered timber opens a gash along your shin.

the-reed-music.label: Salve his salt-burned feet
the-reed-music.intent: Kneel with your medicine and look at the feet he never lifts from the dry ground.
the-reed-music.risk: Salt sores can go deeper than any salve.

success.text: His feet are cracked raw from the salt, and he has not walked in a week; the music was the only way to call anyone. You salve and wrap them, and by evening he can stand and share his dried fish with you.

hammer-under-the-stone.label: Wait for the night cutters
hammer-under-the-stone.intent: Hide by the fresh seam after dark to see who comes to cut without supports.
hammer-under-the-stone.risk: The quarry gets bitter cold once the sun goes.

success.text: Near midnight a line of hollow-cheeked debtors files in with lamps, a company foreman behind them. You count eleven, and you understand now that the quarry's silence was bought.

failure.text: Cold settles into the quarry after dark, and you doze against the stone. You wake at dawn stiff and chilled, to fresh cuts on the seam and nobody in sight.

hammer-under-the-stone.label: Carry the mason's warning down
hammer-under-the-stone.intent: Walk to the laborers' shacks and tell them the seam will kill whoever cuts it next.
hammer-under-the-stone.risk: Frightened workers may hear it as a threat to their wage.

success.text: The laborers listen, and some of them believe you, but the company pays for that seam by the night. At dusk you watch two lamps climb toward it anyway, and the mason shakes his head.

the-empty-pay-cart.label: Take his silence money
the-empty-pay-cart.intent: Accept a share of whatever he has hidden, and agree you never saw the sheet.
the-empty-pay-cart.risk: You will carry those names whether you read them or not.

success.text: He digs a sack of bread and dried beans out from under the pebbles and counts out your share. The pay sheet stays where it is, and as you leave he goes back to counting stones into the cart.

the-empty-pay-cart.label: Put a hand on his collar
the-empty-pay-cart.intent: Take him by the collar and make him say where the wages actually went.
the-empty-pay-cart.risk: Men who handle money keep guards close by.

success.text: He talks fast. The wages went to the night foreman, and the workers' rations are in a sack under the pebbles. You leave the sack at the tunnel mouth for them and keep one loaf for the road.

failure.text: He screams before you can stop him, and his guards come running. You fight your way out bruised and battered, with his hatred following you up the road.

the-glass-vein.label: Pull her back from the seam
the-glass-vein.intent: The singing has changed pitch, so drag her away before the vein lets go.
the-glass-vein.risk: If you are wrong, you have cost her a day's work.

success.text: You haul her back by the arm, and a breath later the whole vein bursts, spraying black glass across the tray. She lives, and everything she cut today is splinters. She thanks you, and then she sits down and cries.

failure.text: You pull her clear just as the vein shatters, but a sliver catches you across the hands. You do not feel it until the blood starts, and by then she is binding the cuts for you.

the-watchful-overhang.label: Walk last in the line
the-watchful-overhang.intent: Take the last place under the shelf so nobody is left alone beneath it.
the-watchful-overhang.risk: The last walker takes whatever the wall lets go.

success.text: The line shuffles through, and you come last. Gravel rattles down onto your back and a stone strikes hard, but every traveler reaches the far side, and the scout nods to you once.

the-watchful-overhang.label: Ask why the wall is moving
the-watchful-overhang.intent: Ask the scout what she thinks is shaking a wall no weather can explain.
the-watchful-overhang.risk: Some answers make the road ahead harder.

success.text: She points at fresh rubble below: someone has been quarrying under the canyon wall at night. Then she leads you up a scouts' path above it, and the trail ahead runs a different way than the one you came for.

failure.text: She looks at you as if you had asked why water is wet, and goes back to watching. You spend the hour craning up at the shelf, and come away tired and no wiser.

the-banner-in-the-wind.label: Ask why the rider left
the-banner-in-the-wind.intent: Ask the captain what her rider was carrying, and whether she had reason to run.
the-banner-in-the-wind.risk: A captain's pride can turn a question into an accusation.

success.text: The rider was carrying debtors' writs, the captain admits, and hated the work. The banner marks the old courier road she took. The captain shows it to you, and the road ahead bends that way too.

failure.text: The captain stiffens and tells you her rider was loyal to the last stitch. She rides off alone, and you are left with the banner snapping overhead and no more than you knew.

the-banner-in-the-wind.label: Leave her food for the search
the-banner-in-the-wind.intent: Press your own food on the captain so she can keep searching past dark.
the-banner-in-the-wind.risk: You will be hungry before the next camp.

success.text: She takes it without arguing, which tells you how long she has gone without. She rides back toward the bridge as the light fails, and you never learn whether she found her rider.

the-toll-without-a-keeper.label: Pay into the empty box
the-toll-without-a-keeper.intent: Drop food in the box although nobody is guarding it, and walk on.
the-toll-without-a-keeper.risk: Paying an unwatched toll may only feed a liar.

success.text: Before you have gone ten steps she is down off the rocks, looking into the box. It feeds her sister's children, she says, since the quarry took her sister. She has nothing to give you back.

the-toll-without-a-keeper.label: Ask about the blunted spear
the-toll-without-a-keeper.intent: Call up to her and ask why anyone would carry a spear she has dulled herself.
the-toll-without-a-keeper.risk: Questions about her past may make her use it.

success.text: She climbs down and tells you she once rode escort for the Canyon Warden, until she was ordered to turn sick travelers back into a storm. Then she lifts the rope and sends you by the escorts' trail, and the road ahead changes.

failure.text: She tells you to mind your own spear and throws a stone that catches you on the shoulder. You go on down the trail bruised, the question unanswered.

one-place-by-the-fire.label: Set bread at the empty place
one-place-by-the-fire.intent: Put some of your own food in the empty seat's bowl, for whoever it waits for.
one-place-by-the-fire.risk: It may sit there untouched while you go hungry.

success.text: Nobody touches it. Near dawn a thin figure slips out of the dark, sits in the empty place, and eats without a word, and the host weeps quietly into the fire. Nobody asks why, and neither do you.

the-map-in-ashes.label: Copy the routes in charcoal
the-map-in-ashes.intent: Grab a stick of charcoal and copy the routes onto cloth faster than she burns them.
the-map-in-ashes.risk: Hasty copies of bad maps can be worse than none.

success.text: You copy three routes before the last map curls black, and one of them shows a trail the others all left out. She watches you work and does not stop you, and the road ahead looks different now.

failure.text: The smoke stings your eyes and the sparks burn your fingers, and what you copy is a smear. You keep it anyway, though you know it will lead you nowhere.

the-map-in-ashes.label: Help her burn them
the-map-in-ashes.intent: Take a stack of maps and feed them to the fire beside her, one by one.
the-map-in-ashes.risk: Some of those routes might have saved someone.

success.text: You burn them together without talking. When the last one is gone she tells you the names of the people each map killed, and you sit with her until the fire is only coals.

the-night-watch-debt.label: Offer your word as surety
the-night-watch-debt.intent: Promise him a night's watch at the next camp, and ask him to trust that you keep promises.
the-night-watch-debt.risk: An old sentry has heard every promise there is.

success.text: He studies your face a long while, then nods and takes the watch. You sleep deep for the first time in days. At dawn he tells you the footsteps he counts belong to the warden's scouts, counting travelers.

failure.text: He has heard too many promises. He shrugs, takes the watch anyway, and leaves you lying awake owing him a night you never agreed to. You rise at dawn tired and uneasy.

feathers-in-the-draft.label: Ask what she paid the cave
feathers-in-the-draft.intent: Ask the storm-reader what bargain let her stand at this threshold untouched.
feathers-in-the-draft.risk: Her answer may be a price you're asked to match.

success.text: Her childhood name, she says, given to the wind forty years ago. In return the draft taught her which passages breathe and which ones swallow. She shows you three of them, scratched in the dust with a feather's quill.

failure.text: She takes the question as an offer and asks for your own name in payment. When you refuse, she turns her back, and you wait an hour in the wind's teeth before she lets you pass, chilled through.

feathers-in-the-draft.label: Climb the ridge path around
feathers-in-the-draft.intent: Refuse her question and climb over the ridge to find another way in.
feathers-in-the-draft.risk: The ridge is bare, and the storm is close.

success.text: The climb is long and cold, and the wind tries to peel you off the rock twice. You come down to a smaller mouth on the far side, and the tunnels beyond it match none of the landmarks you were steering by.

the-third-shadow.label: Pay her brother's debt
the-third-shadow.intent: Offer the trappers your food to clear her brother's debt, so the trap can end.
the-third-shadow.risk: The trappers may take the food and want more.

success.text: The trappers count your sack twice and call it square. The guide cannot meet your eyes when she thanks you, and her brother is not there to thank you at all. She leads you down the honest way in silence.

shelter-for-the-storm.label: Hold the lamp for her
shelter-for-the-storm.intent: Shield the healer's guttering lamp with your body while she sets a broken arm.
shelter-for-the-storm.risk: The wind and the rain will find your back.

success.text: You stand with the lamp inside your coat while she works, and the bone goes in clean. Afterward she gives you a twist of willow bark and a pouch of yarrow, and tells you exactly how much of each to use.

failure.text: A gust gets under your coat and the lamp dies at the worst moment. She finishes by feel, and the arm will mend crooked. By the end you are soaked to the skin and shaking.

shelter-for-the-storm.label: Stand in the floodwater
shelter-for-the-storm.intent: Wade onto the flooding ledge and stand there as a handhold while everyone crosses.
shelter-for-the-storm.risk: The water is rising, and you'll be last across.

success.text: One after another, they cross with a hand on your shoulder, and the water reaches your waist before the last child is over. Nobody stops to thank you; they are too cold. The healer remembers, and tells you quietly that she owes you.

the-candle-court.label: Fetch the missing witness
the-candle-court.intent: Slip out to the tunnels and find the witness who was supposed to come.
the-candle-court.risk: No one is meant to leave while the court sits.

success.text: You find him two tunnels away, hiding; he owes one of the miners money and feared the court would ask. You walk him back, he tells the truth, and the court lets his own debt wait a season for his honesty.

failure.text: The clerks catch you at the edge of the candlelight and hold you through the court's whole session. You go hungry while it drags on, and the adjudicator fines you a day's food for trying to leave.

the-candle-court.label: Pay the salt's worth yourself
the-candle-court.intent: Offer the court your food as the price of the salt, so both miners walk away whole.
the-candle-court.risk: Nobody will ever learn who was lying.

success.text: The adjudicator accepts the trade. Both miners take a pouch and both leave believing they were right. The truth stays buried in the hollow, and your pack is lighter by two days of food.

salt-on-the-threshold.label: Wait out the pressure shift
salt-on-the-threshold.intent: Sit with the mason on the safe side of the salt until the pressure has passed.
salt-on-the-threshold.risk: The shift may last longer than your food.

success.text: It takes most of a day. You eat while you wait and listen to the mason talk about her son, who went down the deep road and never came back. When the air settles, she shows you the old masons' marks that tell a safe passage from a bad one.

salt-on-the-threshold.label: Question her slate
salt-on-the-threshold.intent: Ask the mason to walk you through her slate, line by line, looking for a mistake.
salt-on-the-threshold.risk: She has been right before, and she knows it.

success.text: Her numbers are good, but her dates are wrong; the shift is a day off, not an hour. She swears, laughs, and hands you the slate to carry to the miners on the far side, who will need it.

failure.text: She takes offense and snatches the slate back. While you argue, the pressure turns, and the air by the cracked vent stings your throat raw before you both retreat.

the-forgotten-pledge.label: Stand his watch till dawn
the-forgotten-pledge.intent: Promise to stand before the chamber in his place so he can sleep one night.
the-forgotten-pledge.risk: The charm may not care who stands the watch.

success.text: The charm cools on his wrist while you stand in his place, and he sleeps like a dropped stone. At dawn you wake him as you promised, though your legs are shaking. He is still bound, but he has slept.

the-forgotten-pledge.label: Break the chamber seal
the-forgotten-pledge.intent: Break open the sealed chamber to see what he has guarded all these years.
the-forgotten-pledge.risk: Whatever was sealed in may have wanted to stay.

success.text: The seal cracks, and the chamber is empty but for an old ledger of debts, every one paid. He has guarded nothing for years. He goes on reciting anyway, because the charm leaves him no choice, but now he knows.

failure.text: The seal holds and the charm flares. The guardian's arm drives you back from the door, and you hit the stone hard while he shouts that you nearly made him a traitor to an oath he cannot remember.

three-doors-no-hinges.label: Wait for the next tremor
three-doors-no-hinges.intent: Wait with the architect until the next tremor, and see which arch stays put.

success.text: Hours pass before the ground shrugs. Two arches swing like gates on hinges they do not have; the third stays still. You eat through a day's food waiting, but the road ahead now runs in a new order you can trust.

voices-across-the-rock.label: Break through the stone
voices-across-the-rock.intent: Swing an iron bar at the thinnest part of the stone sheet.
voices-across-the-rock.risk: Breaking rock in thunder brings more rock down.

success.text: The sheet cracks, then splits, and the courier tumbles through in a cloud of grit. He hugs you, letter and all, and tells you which tunnels ahead the thunder has already ruined. The road ahead reorders itself around them.

failure.text: The stone holds and the ceiling does not. A shower of rock catches your shoulder and you back away, ears ringing, while the courier shouts to ask whether you are still alive.

voices-across-the-rock.label: Leave him to find his way
voices-across-the-rock.intent: Call that you can't reach him, and go on before the thunder brings the roof down.
voices-across-the-rock.risk: He may not find his way out alone.

success.text: His voice follows you for a while, asking you to wait, and then the flat copy of his voice follows that. You come out into a dry passage with all your food and none of your peace.

the-red-vial.label: Brew him a sleeping draught
the-red-vial.intent: Steep the herbs you carry into a draught strong enough to let him sleep.
the-red-vial.risk: Sleep may loosen his grip on what the vial holds back.

success.text: He drinks it and sleeps for the first time in days, the vial cradled in both hands. When he wakes, his hands are steady. He gives you the only thing he has, a strip of jerky, and makes you take it.

failure.text: The draught is too weak. He dozes, starts awake screaming, and the vial cracks against the rock. Red smoke stings your eyes and throat before it clears, and the hunger, he says, is still there.

the-red-vial.label: Carry the vial for him
the-red-vial.intent: Take the vial into your own hands so he can rest, whatever it does to you.
the-red-vial.risk: Whatever it holds back may lean on you instead.

success.text: The glass is colder than the cave, and a hunger that is not yours gnaws at you through it. The pilgrim sleeps beside you for half a night. When you give it back his hands are steadier, and yours are not.

the-cooling-stones.label: Hold the caravan back
the-cooling-stones.intent: Stand in the road with a lantern and talk the lead driver into halting until dawn.
the-cooling-stones.risk: Drivers on a deadline don't stop for strangers.

success.text: The lead driver curses you, then sees the faint glow of the seam and reins in. The caravan camps on solid ground until the fissure has opened and settled, and the drivers share a pot of beans with you and the mender.

failure.text: The driver swings wide around your lantern without slowing, and his rear wheel drops into the opening seam. You help heave the wagon free, and something in your back twists as it comes up.

the-cooling-stones.label: Walk on ahead of it
the-cooling-stones.intent: Leave the mender and the caravan to the seam, and get past before it opens.
the-cooling-stones.risk: The caravan will reach the seam without you.

success.text: You cross the warm stones quickly and keep going. Behind you, when the ground finally splits, you hear shouting and the scream of a horse, and you never learn how it ended. The road ahead is quiet.

mirror-in-the-ash.label: Share a meal with her
mirror-in-the-ash.intent: Sit down in the ash with the scavenger and split your food with her.
mirror-in-the-ash.risk: She may take your bread and give nothing back.

success.text: She eats slowly and tells you the letters were written by her sons, from the war beyond the ridge. She has never opened the last three. She thanks you, and you leave her turning the mirror toward the horizon again.

mirror-in-the-ash.label: Look into the mirror
mirror-in-the-ash.intent: Wipe the ash from the glass and look into it, whatever it shows.
mirror-in-the-ash.risk: You may not like what the glass keeps.

success.text: You see only yourself and the black road behind you, every mile of it. The plain fact of how far you have come steadies you, and you walk on stronger than you were.

failure.text: In the dusty glass you think you see faces along the road behind you, people you passed and did not stop for. You cannot look away until the scavenger turns it face down, and you walk on shaken and sleepless.

ashes-at-the-border.label: Go after her comrades
ashes-at-the-border.intent: Follow the trail her comrades took toward water and bring back whatever you find.
ashes-at-the-border.risk: Ash covers tracks fast, and you will be alone out there.

success.text: You find them two miles out, lost in a gully, and they refill your waterskin from theirs. They lead you back by a sheltered wash the ranger never knew, and the road ahead looks different from its far end. The ranger grips your arm and says she owes you.

failure.text: The trail vanishes under fresh ash, and you wander until dark, drinking more of your water than you meant to. You come back empty-handed and parched, and the ranger is still watching the trail.

ashes-at-the-border.label: Slip under the barrier
ashes-at-the-border.intent: Wait until the ranger is watching the trail, then duck under the barrier and go.
ashes-at-the-border.risk: If she turns, she will know your face at every post.

success.text: You go under the pole while her back is turned and are down the far slope before she looks round. Nobody stops you. Nobody mends the horn, either, and the ranger keeps her lonely watch.

failure.text: She turns just as you duck under. Her shout brings no one, but she knows your face now and swears it will be known at every post on the border. You leave at a run and turn your ankle on the scree.

the-last-watchfire.label: Light the second fire
the-last-watchfire.intent: Pile the dry wood high and light a beacon the lost refugees can see from the dark.
the-last-watchfire.risk: A beacon shows raiders the way as well as refugees.

success.text: The beacon roars up, and within the hour the lost refugees stumble in out of the dark. So do the raiders' scouts, who now know where the camp is weakest. The commander has you put outside the gate for the night, and the cold finds you there.

the-last-watchfire.label: Ask why she won't go
the-last-watchfire.intent: Ask the commander quietly why her sabre is still lying by the gate.
the-last-watchfire.risk: Commanders do not like being read by strangers.

success.text: She lost a patrol in that ravine last winter, she says, and has not trusted her own judgment in the dark since. Saying it aloud loosens something. She buckles on the sabre and leads the search herself, and the guards follow her out.

failure.text: She hears pity in your question and orders you off the wall. You spend the night by the gate, cold and unwelcome, listening to calls from the dark that no one answers.

the-closed-infirmary.label: Treat the wounded outside
the-closed-infirmary.intent: Tear up your spare cloth for bandages and tend the wounded waiting in the yard.
the-closed-infirmary.risk: Your own road still has miles of glass in it.

success.text: You bind wounds with strips of your own blanket and boil water over a guard's fire. By dusk the worst of them are resting. No one thinks to thank you; they are too busy arguing about the door.

the-prisoner-of-dusk.label: Make the guards stand back
the-prisoner-of-dusk.intent: Let the guards see you have drawn blood before, and stand where they must go through you.
the-prisoner-of-dusk.risk: Frightened men sometimes strike at what frightens them most.

success.text: They have heard what you did on the road, and they believe it. The spears come down, and the scout gets through dusk without anyone striking him. The commander thanks you in a voice that makes plain she wants you gone by morning.

failure.text: One guard is more frightened of you than of the scout, and he lunges. You turn the spear aside, but it opens your arm, and in the struggle the copper wire cuts deep into the scout's wrist.

the-prisoner-of-dusk.label: Leave it to the commander
the-prisoner-of-dusk.intent: Step back and let the commander decide what the dusk demands.
the-prisoner-of-dusk.risk: Whatever happens next, it happens without you.

success.text: You walk away toward the cookfires. Behind you, as the sun touches the ridge, someone shouts, and then there is a long silence. The commander never tells you what she did, and the guards will not meet your eyes.

the-key-with-no-door.label: Take the key and walk on
the-key-with-no-door.intent: Accept the stone key and walk past the gate without asking what it opens.
the-key-with-no-door.risk: A key handed over this freely may be a weight.

success.text: The archivist sets the key in your palm and folds your fingers over it. As you walk on, the landmarks she described never appear; the road ahead bends a different way than her carvings showed. The key is heavier than stone should be.

a-promise-kept.label: Tell her the duty is done
a-promise-kept.intent: Tell her honestly that she has carried it far enough, and may set it down.
a-promise-kept.risk: She may hear that the whole road was wasted.

success.text: She weeps, then laughs, then lays the sealed letter on a waystone and weights it with a rock. She turns back toward the camp lighter than she has been in years. The letter stays where she left it, and you do not touch it.

failure.text: She hears that the whole road was wasted and snatches the letter back. She walks through the gate alone, too fast, and you press your food on her because it is the only thing she will take from you.

the-price-of-silence.label: Admit you would break it
the-price-of-silence.intent: You have spoken hard truths on the road before; tell her your silence would be a lie.
the-price-of-silence.risk: Honesty this plain can sound like a threat.

success.text: She studies you a long time, as if weighing every hard truth you have already told. Then she unfolds her hands and steps aside, and you pass through the gate bound to nothing but what you have already said.

failure.text: She takes your honesty as a challenge and closes the direct gate. You walk the long way around the wall in the dark and spend food you cannot spare waiting for light.

the-price-of-silence.label: Accept her terms
the-price-of-silence.intent: Give her the promise of silence she asks for, and take the easy passage.
the-price-of-silence.risk: A promise like this one does not wear off.

success.text: She nods as if she expected nothing else. The gate opens smoothly, and the way beyond is short and well swept. Behind you, the people still waiting watch you go, and you find you have nothing to say to them.
